references.text: Both verses illustrate Isaac's physical limitations that make the identity confusion possible.
The contrast between the original trust in v.1 and the doubt/confrontation in v.32 highlights the consequences of the deception.
V.22 unfolds the physical confirmation of the identity that was initiated with the call in v.1.
V.24 is a direct follow-up to Isaac's doubt, which began with the call in v.1.
The contrast between Isaac's call in v.1 and his rejection in v.37 underscores the loss of the birthright.
V.34 shows the painful consequence for Esau of the situation that was initiated in v.1.
V.24 and v.1 share the same dialogue sequence regarding identity testing.
